In brief

I’m a first-year master’s student in Electrical Engineering at Stanford University, working on computer architecture research advised by Prof. Caroline Trippel.

I recently graduated from UC Berkeley with high distinction and high honors across degrees in Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, and Mechanical Engineering. There, I was lucky to be advised by Prof. Chris Fletcher on hardware security research using BOOM, the Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine.

I’ve also interned twice at Apple: first with the Platform Engineering team on FPGA and emulation, then with the CPU RTL team.

In my spare time, I write math problems. I was Tournament Director and Head Problem Writer for the Berkeley Math Tournament, and I now lead problem writing for the Stanford Math Tournament. You can watch some of my past videos.

Fun fact: Sometimes people call me “(W)rite (En)able,” which is where my GitHub username comes from. Other nicknames I’ve picked up since I was a kid include Cactus and Kumquat (put together, they make my Discord username), OneBurger, and Goldenorange.

Research

  • Sep 2026 – present

    High Assurance Computer Architectures Lab, Stanford

    Turning hardware performance counters into an automated reverse-engineering tool that learns the hidden internals of black-box CPUs, enabling new side-channel analysis and verifiable hardware models. Advised by Prof. Caroline Trippel.

  • Dec 2024 – Sep 2026

    SLICE Lab, UC Berkeley

    Implemented Speculative Taint Tracking on the Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine, and built a covert channel for inter-process communication through cache contention and timing. Advised by Prof. Chris Fletcher.

Selected projects

Oct – Dec 2025 EECS 151 ASIC lab

6-stage RISC-V out-of-order-commit CPU with cache (ASIC)

With my partner Chris, I designed a pipelined RISC-V CPU with instruction and data caches and took it through synthesis and place-and-route in the SkyWater 130nm PDK. It was the first fully functional 6-stage out-of-order-commit CPU in the course, and it won the Apple New Silicon Initiative design contest, which was presented at Apple Park.

Read the full project page

Oct – Dec 2024 EECS 151 FPGA lab

3-stage RISC-V superscalar CPU with branch predictor (FPGA)

With my partner Nikki, I built a 3-stage pipelined RISC-V CPU in Verilog on the Xilinx PYNQ-Z1 at 100 MHz. On my own, I then designed a dual-issue superscalar core that reached a CPI of 0.975. It is the first and only fully functional superscalar CPU in the lab’s history, and it won the Apple New Silicon Initiative design contest, which was presented at Apple Park.

Read the full project page

Sep 2020 – May 2023 Patent #202023061241.7

Sugar-control chopsticks

Chopsticks with a camera and sensors that estimate the sugar content of food and give real-time feedback, to help people with or at risk of diabetes manage what they eat.

More projects

Course and team projects, most recent first.

  • Spring 2026

    Pixel Mirror ME 235

    A real-time computer-vision art piece that turns people walking by into pixel art on a 64×64 LED panel. YOLOv8 segments each person’s silhouette, and an ESP32 drives the panel over a framed, CRC-checked serial link at 25–30 fps. I built the fingertip “gloving” mode with MediaPipe, tracking up to ten fingertips as colored dots, and designed its protocol payload. Watch the video Read more

  • Fall 2025

    E-LEGION passive walker ME 139

    A gravity-powered, four-legged walker inspired by TARS from Interstellar. Designed a four-bar knee that locks during stance and swings freely otherwise, tuned mass placement with tungsten weights, and modeled the Lagrangian dynamics in MATLAB. Read more

    EcoCompressor ME 102B

    A motorized trash-compaction attachment that latches onto a standard trash can. A lead-screw plunger compresses up to 5 kg and cuts volume by 75%, with a photoresistor interlock so it only runs when mounted. Read more

    Tip effects in cross-flow heat transfer ME 103

    An experiment measuring how specimen length changes the convection coefficient of aluminum bars in cross-flow, using a thermal camera and a 3D-printed test rig. Compared 18 trials against Ansys Fluent simulations with uncertainty propagation and z-tests, showing results converge to infinite-length theory as bars get longer. Read more

  • Fall 2024

    IoT smart pillbox ME 100

    An ESP32 pillbox with LED and email reminders, temperature and humidity monitoring on an Adafruit IO dashboard, and a motorized lid that opens one compartment per button press. Watch the video Read more
